text:
maria: quick check — i'm swapping my night shift with @aj tonight. need to make sure primary/secondary roles are explicit and there's no coverage gap before 02:00 UTC. i'm primary until 00:30, aj takes over at 00:45. gap is 15m unless we confirm a warm handoff.

aj: i'm good to take primary at 00:45. can we get a warm handoff in #oncall-bridge at 00:40? i'll be on phone and slack.

maria: yes planning to join bridge at 00:40. leaving runbooks pinned. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/oncall-shift-swap — scroll to "warm handoff".

devon: copying fallback rules here for visibility. if primary unresponsive during takeover window, secondary should assume with a 5-min page to the primary and then escalate at +10m.

sara: can we confirm paging targets for severity levels? i remember we updated the matrix last month.

ops-bot: automated reminder — scheduled shift swap: maria -> aj (00:45 UTC). Bridge reservation created: #oncall-bridge.

maria: paging rules quick summary (from runbook):
- P0 (service down / large customer impact): page primary, then page @sre-lead and on-call manager within 2 minutes. if no ack in 5m, escalate to exec pager.
- P1 (major degradation, partial impact): page primary and secondary immediately. escalate to SRE lead at +10m if unresolved.
- P2 (minor degradation / queued errors): notify primary via slack only; page if error rate persists >30m.

aj: can we add explicit phone number pages for P0? last time SMS delivery delayed. who is on the exec pager?

sre-lead: exec pager list is in vault -> ops/exec-pager. default is oncall-manager then engineering director. for tonight i'm reachable on mobile. i'll join bridge if paged.

devon: copying escalation snippet for quick paste:```
P0: /page primary, wait 2m, /page sre-lead, /page oncall-manager -> if no ack 5m -> /page exec-pager
P1: /page primary + secondary -> +10m page sre-lead
P2: slack notify -> page if >30m ongoing
```

sara: question on customer impact assessment: if a subset of requests (3% of traffic) sees 5s latency increase but error rate stable, is that P1 or P2?

aj: that's borderline. apply the triage: if latency increase causes user-visible failures or violates SLA for paid customers, treat as P1. otherwise P2 and monitor with alerts. document the decision in the incident thread.

maria: i'll make the call if it happens during my window and tag product for SLA confirmation.

incident-bot: detected spike: model-inference latency 99p jumped to 4.9s for 00:10–00:25 UTC. alert severity: elevated. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2030002

aj: i'm taking a look now. starting with routing logs and cache hit rates. joining bridge.

maria: if you need to escalate, page the secondary immediately and use the "fallback-model" routing rule to reduce CPU pressure:```
# quick mitigation
route-policy set default -> lower-capacity-variant
cache flush prefix user-ctx
```

devon: note: do not swap primary while an active incident is open unless both of you are on the bridge and confirm in-thread.

aj: ack. joining bridge, will post updates. if i don't ack in 2m, page me and then @devon.

maria: confirmed — warm handoff scheduled, bridge at 00:40, paging matrix and phone escalation noted. i'll update ops log after swap. :thumbsup:

sara: thanks both. will monitor customer-facing channels and prepare the impact blurb template.

aj: resolved for now — root cause was a routing miskey, rollback to previous route fixed 99p latency. we left mitigation steps in the incident page. closing note: if you see similar pattern, start with route rollback not model restart.

incident-bot: incident INC-2030002 marked RESOLVED by aj at 00:58 UTC.

maria: thanks — swap proceeds as planned. aj, i'll DM phone numbers for direct paging. devon, sara — cheers for backup.

devon: noted. leaving final checklist:
- confirm bridge attendance at 00:40
- verify page targets in PagerDuty for tonight
- run post-incident blameless review if customer impact >5%

aj: all set on my end. good handoff.

maria: end thread — swap complete and coverage confirmed."
